title: How much dimension does an epsilon-approximation to a non-attained quantum correlation cost? A Diophantine answer for K_5
description: The Dykema-Paulsen-Prakash proof that C_q(5,2) is not closed, via a K_5 graph correlation function, is existential in dimension: the finite-dimensional carriers it invokes live in M_k 'for some natural number k', with no control on k and no approximating sequence, rate or carrier at the non-attained parameter. This paper answers the quantitative question that leaves open. Writing D(eps) for the least block dimension of a finite-dimensional carrier whose value exceeds the infimum by at most eps, at exact marginals and at t = 1/sqrt(5), it proves D(eps) = Theta(eps^(-1/4)) in every dimension convention and shows the exponent is arithmetic rather than dynamical in origin. The lower bound (Theorem A) is unconditional, with no block-scalar or equal-rank hypothesis: it runs the Diophantine inequality ||q sqrt(5)|| > 1/(5q) through the law of total variance, giving Q eps^(1/4) > 0.4472135955. For a two-block carrier the deficit is exactly the product of the two one-sided approximation errors, and consecutive continued-fraction convergents of sqrt(5) give an explicit family with N eps^(1/4) -> 0.9732489895 (Theorem B). In the denominator convention the minimum is exact, e_Q = (a_Q - sqrt5)(sqrt5 - b_Q) with Farey neighbours of order Q; the sharp liminf and limsup of D_den(eps) eps^(1/4) are 0.7434960689 and 1.5747499445, and D_den <= D <= 2 D_den. A supporting-line inequality proves this minimum for every carrier, including non-scalar and many-block ones, and two scalar neighbour blocks attain it; the liminf is approached along intermediate semiconvergent pairs (Q = 21, 89, 377, ...), so the convergent value 0.9732489895 is valid but not optimal. The same inequality determines the fixed-target drift threshold exactly: a carrier with reduced denominators at most Q, marginal drift at most delta and deficit at most eps exists if and only if e_Q <= eps + 5(a_Q + b_Q - 1) delta. Hence D(eps, delta) = Theta(min(eps^(-1/4), delta^(-1/4))), with pure-drift liminf constant 0.3642394613 (limsup 0.7714715591). At phi the corresponding sharp constants are 0.8506508084 and 1.3763819205: higher than at sqrt5 in the best case and lower in the worst. Two structural results accompany the law: orbit topology and attainment are different invariants on this object (lambda = 4/3 is attained and has an orbit conjugate to that of the unattained sqrt(5), with the same multiplier), and the analogous cost for I3322 is only logarithmic, so dimension laws for non-closure witnesses are governed by the arithmetic of the parameter and not by a universal rate. Five exact-arithmetic engines (two added in v1.1.0) check the numbered arithmetic claims and confirm the new theorems on finite ranges: the original three (48 + 6 + 4 assertions, exit 0) certify the convergent table by two engines sharing no number representation, with the one shared ingredient disclosed; the two Farey engines, in exact quadratic-field arithmetic and certified rational intervals, agree on all 42,519 straddling pairs per objective at orders 1-12 and on every neighbour-change node through order 300,000. The complete refereeing record - two refutation-first blind rounds either side of a repair round, with mutation testing and freeze checks - ships in-repository under review/.
notes: Version 1.1.0 (2026-11-11) adds the exact Farey law in the denominator convention (Theorem B1), the sharp limiting constants 0.7434960689 and 1.5747499445 (Corollary B2), the exact fixed-target drift criterion e_Q <= eps + 5(a_Q + b_Q - 1) delta with pure-drift liminf constant 0.3642394613 (Theorem 5.3(b,c)), the sharp comparison with phi (0.8506508084 and 1.3763819205), and two independent verification engines. It corrects three v1.0.2 sentences that were false as written: Sections 4.1 and 5.3 called the continued-fraction convergents the extremisers (at Q = 21 the optimum is the Farey pair (47/21, 38/17)), and Section 5.2 called the consecutive convergent deficit ratio the exact fixed factor (2+sqrt5)^4 (it is only the limit). Theorem A, Theorem B's convergent family and the v1.0.2 drift correction remain valid. Earlier corrections: v1.0.1 (2026-08-25) corrected Section 7.2; v1.0.2 (2026-09-24) refuted the Section 5.3 drift Open Lemma.
